title: Task
description: The task the model hands in. The language is an argument of the call, not a field here. Trap ids, five different options and a distractor for every wrong option are checked by the service, not by this schema.

core_idea.description: The mathematical core before the plot: the idea, and why the answer is what it is.

design_thought_process.description: How the plot and the traps were chosen. Shown to nobody; it makes the reasoning explicit before the task is committed to.

question.description: The wording the child reads, in the language of the chat.

drawing.description: Optional text drawing, lines separated by newlines. It comes together with drawing_structure.

hint.description: One leading question or the first step, given on request before the child answers. It must not give the answer away.

solution.description: Step by step, in the words a tutor would use with a child of that grade. The child sees it after answering.

distractors.description: One entry for each of the four wrong options, and none for the correct one.

distractor.description: A wrong option: the mistake it comes from, and what the child is told after choosing it.

trap.description: Trap id from the trap catalog: the mistake that leads to this option.

text.description: What the child reads after choosing this option. It names the mistake rather than retelling the solution.

drawing_structure.description: The same picture as data, so that the drawing can be compared with the wording without either being understood.

kind.description: What is drawn, such as number_line, grid, balance, pouring or clock.

objects.description: What the drawing shows: an id, the label exactly as it appears in the drawing, and a value where the object has one.

relations.description: How the objects stand to each other, as triples such as left_of from A to B.
